root_cause.text: The etas_es58x driver’s es58x_alloc_rx_urbs() incorrectly returned an error after partially allocating and anchoring RX URBs, even though partial allocation is valid, causing es58x_open() to abort before the free_urbs cleanup path and leak the anchored URBs.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message states that “when es58x_alloc_rx_urbs() fails to allocate the requested number of URBs but succeeds in allocating some, it returns an error code,” which makes “es58x_open() return early, skipping the cleanup label ‘free_urbs’, which leads to the anchored URBs being leaked”; the patch changes the function’s final return from “return ret;” to “return 0;”.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return success explicitly from es58x_alloc_rx_urbs() on the successful allocation path to avoid propagating an incorrect ret value.
intent_record.what: The function es58x_alloc_rx_urbs() was changed so that its final return statement returns the constant 0 instead of returning the variable ret.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when the function reaches this successful completion path after allocating RX URBs and logging the debug message, it now always reports success instead of propagating the current value of ret, which may contain a stale or unrelated error code. This prevents false failure reporting on successful allocation.

candidates.rationale: This returns the last allocation status variable on the normal exit path even after partial RX URB allocation has succeeded. Because ret can still hold an error value from a failed later allocation attempt, es58x_open() aborts and the already anchored URBs are leaked.

vuln_statements.explanation: In es58x_alloc_rx_urbs(), this statement incorrectly propagates the last allocation status on the normal success path. After partial RX URB allocation and anchoring, ret may still contain an error from a later failed allocation attempt even though partial allocation is acceptable. Returning that error causes es58x_open() to abort before the cleanup path, leaking the already anchored URBs.

    can: etas_es58x: add core support for ETAS ES58X CAN USB interfaces

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `es58x_alloc_rx_urbs()` and `es58x_open()`, so the snippet is sufficient. In `es58x_alloc_rx_urbs()`, the loop allocates, anchors, and submits RX URBs: `usb_anchor_urb(urb, &es58x_dev->rx_urbs);` and after successful submission `usb_free_urb(urb);`. If allocation/submission later fails after some earlier URBs succeeded, the function breaks out of the loop with `ret` still holding the error from the failed iteration. Then after the loop it does: `if (i == 0) ... return ret; ... return ret;`. This means even when `i > 0` (partial allocation succeeded), it still returns the failure code instead of success. That matches the root cause: partial allocation is treated as an error. In `es58x_open()`, the caller does `ret = es58x_alloc_rx_urbs(es58x_dev); if (ret) return ret;` on the first opened channel. Because it returns immediately here, it does not go through the later `free_urbs:` cleanup label, so any previously anchored RX URBs remain leaked. The fix is not present because there is no logic to convert partial success into success (e.g. return 0 when `i > 0`), and `es58x_open()` still aborts immediately on any nonzero return from `es58x_alloc_rx_urbs()`.
